title: Compute-Matched Evaluation Reveals Task-Dependent Diffusion Planning Advantage

contributions.purpose: Enable a fair comparison between diffusion and autoregressive language models that isolates the generation paradigm from inference budget.
contributions.mechanism: A compute-matched evaluation protocol that calibrates autoregressive best-of-k sampling so that k*t_AR matches the diffusion model's wall-clock time per instance (k = floor(t_diffusion / t_AR)), measured on a held-out calibration set.
contributions.evaluation: Applied on A100-80GB where Dream-7B takes 48-56s/instance vs Qwen2.5-7B 1.4s/instance, yielding k=35 (Countdown) and k=39 (Mini Sudoku); robustness checked with median vs p75 timing estimators.
contributions.domain: Evaluation methodology for planning/reasoning language models (diffusion vs autoregressive)
contributions.source_quote: A compute-matched evaluation protocol using wall-clock calibrated best-of-k sampling for fair comparison between diffusion and autoregressive language models.

contributions.purpose: Determine whether diffusion's reported planning advantage survives compute matching.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluate Dream-7B (diffusion) against its autoregressive initializer Qwen2.5-7B under greedy, compute-matched best-of-k, and diffusion conditions on two Reasoning Gym tasks (Countdown, Mini Sudoku).
contributions.evaluation: Task-dependent result: on Countdown compute-matched AR beats Dream by 32.5pp (39.1% vs 6.6%); on Mini Sudoku Dream retains 10.4pp advantage (77.6% vs 67.2%, 95% CI [+6.1, +14.6]).
contributions.domain: Planning tasks (sequential arithmetic vs constraint satisfaction)
contributions.source_quote: Empirical evidence that diffusion's planning advantage is task-specific: absent on sequential arithmetic (Countdown) but significant on constraint satisfaction (Mini Sudoku).

contributions.purpose: Explain the structural basis of the task-dependent advantage.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis via scaling curves (accuracy vs k) and problem-structure interpretation, linking diffusion's bidirectional/iterative refinement to global-coherence tasks and AR sampling diversity to sequential tasks.
contributions.evaluation: On Countdown AR surpasses Dream at k=4 (11% of budget, no saturation); on Mini Sudoku log-linear extrapolation estimates k~87 (2.2x budget) needed to match Dream.
contributions.domain: Analysis of generation-paradigm advantages by problem structure
contributions.source_quote: Analysis suggesting diffusion may excel at tasks requiring global coherence across simultaneous constraints, while autoregressive models with sufficient sampling dominate on tasks with sequential structure.

self_declared_provenance.quote: These works consistently compare diffusion models against greedy autoregressive decoding, leaving open the question of whether the observed advantages persist under compute-matched conditions.

Self-consistency (Wang et al., 2022) showed that sampling diverse reasoning paths and selecting the most consistent answer yields significant gains over greedy decoding ... These inference-time techniques demonstrate that autoregressive models can substantially improve through increased compute, motivating our compute-matched evaluation framework.
Our work bridges these lines of research by directly comparing how diffusion and autoregressive models scale with inference compute on planning tasks.

We compare Dream-7B (Ye et al., 2025), a 7.6B-parameter diffusion language model initialized from Qwen2.5-7B, against its autoregressive initializer Qwen2.5-7B (Yang et al., 2024). Both models share the same architecture and parameter count, differing only in their generation paradigm.

notes: Reports a task-dependent/mixed result: compute-matched AR dominates diffusion on Countdown (-32.5pp for diffusion) while diffusion retains an advantage on Mini Sudoku; greedy AR and diffusion are near-parity on Countdown (6.0% vs 6.6%).
